title: Finite-Sample Certification of Causal Representation Learning under Gaussian Variance-Reset Interventions
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS, but paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4 capped the sound package at subfield below the field floor; no faithful bounded repair exists.
gap_reasons: The positive theorem delivers finite-sample recover-or-abstain certification only for linear Gaussian perfect variance resets under known, transcript-defined population bands; it neither extends to the broader smooth-intervention class nor derives those bands from more primitive law conditions.

The logistic converse proves an exact no-return result at one explicit null, but establishes only the necessity of excluding some weak graph-changing alternatives, not necessity of the proposed bands or a quantitative minimax beta-min boundary.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a sound transcript-local Gaussian recover-or-abstain certificate, a polynomial-bit post-summary realization, an explicit separation family, and a bounded-kernel logistic no-return boundary; the D0.5 mathematics review passed. The package nevertheless missed the field floor because its positive theorem remains confined to a perfect-variance-reset Gaussian subclass with declared bands, while the converse is not a matched quantitative minimax boundary and the implementation is not end-to-end from raw data. No Lean formalization was entered.
tldr: As an exact-real statistical procedure on the declared linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset class, the certificate returns the environment-labelled transitive closure \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and an environment-indexed encoder estimate within \(\tau\) of the parent-supported population range class, or abstains. Its per-environment sample dependence is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), up to the displayed logarithms, and rational post-summary decisions have a proved polynomial-bit realization. The encoder output is neither asserted invertible nor a unique representative of a repeated positive eigenspace. A separate explicit bounded-kernel logistic family gives the intrinsic boundary: if a model class contains graph-changing alternatives converging to its empty-graph null in every finite-prefix total variation, every uniformly \(\alpha\)-valid randomized sequential rule returns the correct singleton empty graph there with probability at most \(\alpha\). Thus some restriction excluding such weak alternatives is necessary for high-probability finite singleton certification, while public reached gaps are one sufficient restriction on the Gaussian class; the theorem does not make the particular \(g_0,h_0\) parameters necessary, establish a minimax rate, or show failure of a named published workflow. Separately, a legal all-dimension Gaussian family has constant reached gaps but a positive unqueried equation-(22) margin that vanishes exponentially, proving no positive dimension-uniform constant lower bound on that margin is necessary and that the corresponding sufficient sample analysis is exponentially pessimistic on this family without contradicting its existential premise.
gap: Acartürk et al.'s finite-sample graph-recovery premise combines equation (22)'s global all-subset margin \(\eta^{\ast}\), equation (23)'s printed norm-product scale \(\gamma^{\ast}\), Assumption 1, smooth full-support models, distinct interventions, and consistent score estimation. Its rank analysis still pays for every subset although the deterministic program executes only a polynomial transcript, and its printed norm product must not be identified with the reciprocal lower bound furnished by actual projector geometry.
fill: The project proves a permutation-equivariant transcript-local certificate and, on the common subregion satisfying the reached projector band, a strict all-dimension relaxation of the source's equation (22) premise while retaining its printed equation (23) threshold condition and every non-margin side condition. The reciprocal quantity \(\rho_i(G)\) is reported separately as a valid lower bound, not imposed as a new class assumption. Certified polynomial-bit spectral composition remains the first-class open question.
